FN-QVQT444-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 1
Committee: Ports, Waterways & Intermodal Sponsor: Representative Chip Brown
Transit
Analyst: Cary Dean Date: 02/19/2025
House Bill 1 as reported by the Committee on Ports, Waterways & Intermodal Transit would
create the Imported Seafood Safety Fund in the State Treasury to fund the inspection, analysis,
sampling, and monitoring of imported seafood products by the Department of Public Health.
This bill would increase the obligations to the department by a department-estimated amount of
$26,000 annually.
Additionally, this bill would increase receipts to the fund by assessing an "imported seafood
safety fee" of $500 for residents and $700 for non-residents to be paid as provided by this bill.
The Department of Conservation and Natural Resources issued 694 seafood dealer licenses in
2024.

FN-QVQT444-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 1
Committee: Ports, Waterways & Intermodal Sponsor: Brown
Transit
Analyst: Cary Dean Date: 02/10/2025
House Bill 1 as introduced would create the Imported Seafood Safety Fund in the State Treasury
to fund the inspection, analysis, sampling, and monitoring of imported seafood products by the
Department of Public Health. This bill would increase the obligations to the department by a
department-estimated amount of $26,000 annually.
Additionally, this bill would increase receipts to the fund by $200 for each "imported seafood
safety fee" paid as provided by this bill. The Department of Conservation and Natural Resources
issued 694 seafood dealer licenses in 2024.

FN-QVQT444-3
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 1
Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Sponsor: Representative Chip Brown
Economic Development
Analyst: Cary Dean Date: 04/09/2025
House Bill 1 as passed the House of Representatives would increase resident and nonresident
seafood dealer licenses and seafood dealer vehicle licenses by $200 per license, which, based
upon the 694 licenses issued in calendar year 2024 by the Department of Conservation and
Natural Resources (DCNR), would generate an estimated $139,000 annually to be remitted by
DCNR to Sweet Grown Alabama to promote the state's seafood products.

FN-QVQT444-4
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 1
Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Sponsor: Representative Chip Brown
Economic Development
Analyst: Cary Dean Date: 04/10/2025
House Bill 1 as reported by the Committee on Fiscal Responsibility and Economic
Development would increase resident seafood dealer licenses by $265 per license, nonresident
seafood dealer licenses by $330 per license, and seafood dealer vehicle licenses by $233 per
license, which, based upon the 694 licenses issued in calendar year 2024, by the Department of
Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR), would increase receipts to DCNR by an
estimated $182,000. Of this amount, $139,000 would be remitted by DCNR to Sweet Grown
Alabama, pursuant to the provisions of this bill, to promote the state's seafood products; and the
remaining $43,000 would be used by DCNR for the administration of its Division of Marine
Resources.
